plan:
FULL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing has been executed and no numerical outcomes are claimed)

(a) OBJECTIVE AND HYPOTHESES (stated as questions, not predictions)

Objective: Determine how well the QuaRot rotation-based quantization pipeline (Ashkboos et al., NeurIPS 2024) generalizes beyond LLaMA-family models to Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct, and how QuaRot-RTN compares to QuaRot-GPTQ at INT4, INT6, and INT8 weight-and-activation quantization.

Primary questions:
Q1. Does the QuaRot rotation pipeline, ported to Phi3ForCausalLM, produce perplexity and zero-shot accuracy at each bit-width that behaves qualitatively like its published LLaMA results (i.e., near-baseline at INT8, small degradation at INT4)?
Q2. Within each bit-width, what is the RTN-vs-GPTQ gap in perplexity and mean zero-shot accuracy on Phi-3-mini, and does the relative ordering match the pattern the paper reports for LLaMA (GPTQ ≥ RTN, with the gap largest at 4 bits)?
Q3. How does the degradation-vs-bit-width curve on Phi-3-mini compare, design-level, against the published LLaMA-2/3 reference points from the paper — i.e., is there evidence of architecture-specific generalization failure (e.g., at INT4)?

Note: these are comparison questions; the design-level "comparison against published LLaMA reference points" is qualitative (trend/ordinal comparison), not a controlled same-hardware reproduction.

(b) MODEL AND METHOD CONFIGURATION TABLE (6-cell grid + FP16 baseline)

All cells use the same ported QuaRot rotation pipeline on microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct (3.8B). Bit-widths apply to both weights (W) and activations (A) in the core grid; group size 128.

| Cell | Model | Rotations | Method | W-bits | A-bits | Group size | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | Phi-3-mini-4k | — | — | FP16 | FP16 | — | Unquantized reference |
| R1 | Phi-3-mini-4k | ON | RTN | 4 | 4 | 128 | Core |
| R2 | Phi-3-mini-4k | ON | RTN | 6 | 6 | 128 | Core |
| R3 | Phi-3-mini-4k | ON | RTN | 8 | 8 | 128 | Core |
| R4 | Phi-3-mini-4k | ON | GPTQ | 4 | 4 | 128 | Core |
| R5 | Phi-3-mini-4k | ON | GPTQ | 6 | 6 | 128 | Core |
| R6 | Phi-3-mini-4k | ON | GPTQ | 8 | 8 | 128 | Core |
| Optional E1/E2 | Phi-3-mini-4k | ON | RTN / GPTQ | 4/6/8 | FP16 | 128 | Weight-only extension (post-approval only; attributes the RTN/GPTQ gap to activation quantization) |

Source-anchored method configuration (anchored to official repo defaults, per your U3 decision; each item is an assumption, not a verified fact): Hadamard rotations at all online-rotation sites (input embedding/first-layer input, attention Q/K/V inputs with fused "rotate-half" style rotation for RoPE compatibility, attention output/MLP down-proj inputs, plus offline rotations of weights where the repo applies them); per-channel asymmetric quantization with group size 128; GPTQ ordered block-wise with activation statistics for column ordering; standard per-layer output-magnitude clipping search for RTN/GPTQ as in the repo. Rotation machinery is identical in R1–R6; only the quantizer bit-widths change.

(c) CALIBRATION AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL

Calibration (identical for RTN and GPTQ, fixed seed S=0 unless repo convention dictates otherwise — flagged in the assumptions register):
- Source: WikiText-2 training split; 512 sequences of length 2048 tokens (paper-canonical), sampled once, cached, and reused for every quantized cell so method differences cannot be confounded with calibration differences.
- GPTQ uses the same calibration data for Hessian/activation collection; RTN uses none beyond what the repo's clipping search consumes (if the repo's clip search uses calibration statistics, the same 512-sequence set is used).

Perplexity evaluation:
- WikiText-2 test split and C4 validation split, sequence length 2048, standard stride/no-overlap tokenization as in the paper's evaluation scripts; report perplexity per benchmark per cell.

Zero-shot evaluation (full six-task suite, per your decision; lm-evaluation-harness):
- LAMBADA-OpenAI (accuracy), HellaSwag (accuracy-normalized), PiQA (accuracy), Winogrande (accuracy), ARC-easy and ARC-challenge (accuracy), plus the unweighted mean over the six tasks. Task versions/harness commit pinned in the run configuration.

Seeds and determinism: fixed seeds for calibration sampling, GPTQ ordering initialization, and harness decoding-greedy defaults; every cell logged with model revision hash, code commit, harness commit, and config dump.

(d) CONTROLS

Held constant across R1–R6: the ported rotation pipeline (all Hadamard sites), group size (128), calibration set and seed, evaluation tokenization and sequence length, harness tasks and versions, hardware and batch settings.
Varies: only quantization method (RTN vs GPTQ) and bit-width (4/6/8).
Isolation logic:
- Within a bit-width, R4−R1, R5−R2, R6−R3 isolate the GPTQ-vs-RTN effect.
- Within a method, R2−R1 / R3−R2 (and GPTQ analogues) isolate bit-width effects.
- The full Phi-3 grid vs the paper's published LLaMA numbers isolates (design-level) the generalization question: same method, same nominal protocol, different architecture.
- R0 provides the FP16 delta denominator for every cell (perplexity delta and per-task accuracy drop).

(e) ANALYSIS PLAN

1. Primary table: for each of the 7 rows (R0–R6), perplexity on WikiText-2 and C4, six per-task zero-shot accuracies, and mean zero-shot accuracy.
2. Delta tables: ΔPPL = PPL(cell)/PPL(R0) (relative) and ΔPPL_abs; ΔAcc per task and mean. Present as a 2(method) × 3(bits) matrix of deltas.
3. Method comparison: for each bit-width, report RTN vs GPTQ deltas; examine whether the gap shrinks monotonically with bit-width (expected pattern from the paper's LLaMA results — treated as a trend to check, not an outcome to claim).
4. Bit-width comparison: degradation curves (bits on x-axis) per method per metric.
5. Generalization comparison: side-by-side design-level comparison against the paper's published LLaMA-2/3-7B QuaRot-RTN and QuaRot-GPTQ 4-bit results (6-bit/8-bit have no published LLaMA counterparts — this asymmetry is stated explicitly). Ordinal/trend comparison only: does Phi-3-mini show the same qualitative behavior at INT4, and does its absolute/relative degradation fall in a similar range? Any conclusion would be phrased as "consistent with / differs from the published LLaMA pattern," never as a reproduction.
6. Robustness notes: (i) clipping-range re-tuning at INT6/INT8 — 4-bit-tuned clipping ranges may be suboptimal at higher widths; if any per-width clipping search is performed, it must use the identical search procedure, calibration data, and budget for both RTN and GPTQ so the method comparison stays fair; the chosen policy (search per bit-width vs single global policy) is recorded as a configuration decision. (ii) If the optional weight-only extension is run, the RTN-vs-GPTQ gap under W-only quantization is used to attribute the core-grid gap to activation quantization.

(f) FEASIBILITY AND RISKS

Compute estimate (order of magnitude, for the eventual run environment — not this sandbox): Phi-3-mini (3.8B, FP16 ≈ 8 GB weights) quantization plus GPTQ Hessian collection fits comfortably on a single 24–40 GB GPU; 7 cells × (1 quantization run + 2 perplexity evals + 6 zero-shot tasks) is on the order of a few GPU-hours to ~a day, dominated by zero-shot evaluation. No multi-GPU requirement.

Porting risk (U1/U2 — feasibility-risk section per your decision; nothing asserted as fact about the official repo's contents):
- What must be checked in the QuaRot code before the run: (i) which model classes the rotation-surgery supports (LLaMA-family confirmed by the paper; whether Phi3ForCausalLM is present in the repo or a fork is unknown and must be verified); (ii) Phi-3's QKV bias terms — the rotation surgery must be adapted so that rotations remain output-preserving when biases are present (bias handling must be derived from the repo's LLaMA path rather than assumed); (iii) fused QKV layout — Phi-3's packed QKV projection differs from LLaMA's separate q/k/v projections, so the fused rotation at attention inputs may need a new code path; (iv) the 4k variant's RoPE path (dense attention, no LongRoPE scaling) — verify the fused rotate/rotate-half interaction matches Phi-3's rotary implementation.
- Gate: a pre-quantization numerical check — FP16 Phi-3-mini with rotations applied vs unrotated FP16 must match in perplexity to within tolerance — before any quantized cell is run. This is the go/no-go test for the port.
- Mitigation if surgery fails: fall back to comparing against the paper's weight-only or partial-rotation configurations, or scope the result as "QuaRot-generalization blocked by architecture-specific surgery" — itself an informative finding for Q1.

Other risks and fallbacks:
- U4 (6/8-bit fake-quant): if activation fake-quant at higher widths behaves unexpectedly, first check clipping policy (see e.6); the fallback is weight-only W6/W8 with FP16 activations, clearly marked as a protocol deviation.
- Runtime fallback (permitted but secondary): if zero-shot runtime is infeasible, reduce to three tasks (LAMBADA, HellaSwag, ARC-e) and mark the deviation explicitly; the primary design keeps all six.
- Calibration sensitivity (A2): if time permits, one repeat with a different calibration seed at INT4-GPTQ only, to bound seed sensitivity; optional, not part of the core grid.
- Environment: the design assumes a run environment with network access (HF model/datasets) and a GPU; the current design sandbox has neither, which is acceptable because this task is design-only.

(g) ASSUMPTIONS REGISTER

Inherited (A1–A5, restated with status):
- A1 (assumption): QuaRot's rotation pipeline can be ported output-preservingly to Phi3ForCausalLM via surgery analogous to its LLaMA implementation. Feasibility gated by the numerical check in (f).
- A2 (assumption): Paper-canonical calibration — 512 sequences × 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train, fixed seed — is the intended protocol; exact sample count/seed to be confirmed against repo defaults.
- A3 (assumption): INT6/INT8 are design extensions beyond the paper's published 4-bit focus; no published Phi-3 or 6/8-bit reference numbers exist for direct comparison.
- A4 (assumption): lm-evaluation-harness task definitions/versions match those used for the paper's zero-shot numbers, enabling design-level comparison.
- A5 (assumption): The eventual run environment provides a single GPU (≥24 GB) and network access to HF assets; not true of this design sandbox, and not required for the deliverable.

New assumptions (all source-anchored to repo defaults per your U3 decision; none verified):
- A6: Group size 128 and per-channel asymmetric quantization are the repo defaults for the core configuration.
- A7: Rotation sites and their placement follow the repo's LLaMA implementation (embedding-input, QKV-input fused, attention-out, MLP-down); porting preserves this placement for Phi-3.
- A8: GPTQ parameters (block ordering, dampening/percent defaults) follow repo defaults rather than paper-text values where they differ.
- A9: Phi-3-mini-4k uses dense (non-sliding) attention, so no sliding-window handling is needed in the port; the 128k/LongRoPE variant is out of scope.
- A10: Clipping-search policy is defined once in the run configuration and applied identically to RTN and GPTQ at every bit-width (policy choice recorded; see e.6).

Every quantity above is a design specification anchored to stated sources; nothing has been run, and no results — actual or illustrative-presented-as-findings — are claimed.
